summary:
A.R.T.E.M.I.S. is an offline-first daily astronaut health, nutrition, and triage assistant built for non-medical crew—engineers, pilots, and scientists—operating on the ISS, deep-space transit, the Moon, and Mars.

To address the challenge of spaceflight health monitoring, the app translates roughly 50 physical, vital-sign, mental-health, diet, and menstrual or suppression metrics into plain-English guidance, step-by-step sensor placement visuals, and an interactive 3D anatomical body map. Each reading is evaluated against environment-adapted baselines using both a Normal/Drift/Critical status system and a 1–7 severity gauge, adjusting recommended actions based on the medical tools available at the crew's exact location (such as a lunar base versus a compact rover). Crew members can also log meals, spot early trends across 14- to 90-day charts, and build daily check-in streaks.

This matters because radio messages between Mars and Earth take up to 22 minutes each way, preventing real-time ground support during medical events. Running completely offline in any browser with zero server setup, A.R.T.E.M.I.S. empowers astronauts to catch early health drift and act autonomously.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

A.R.T.E.M.I.S. is an offline-first daily astronaut health, nutrition, and autonomous triage assistant built for crew operating in Low Earth Orbit (ISS 0g), deep-space transit (0g), the Moon (base and rover, 0.166g), and Mars (0.38g).

The application tracks roughly 50 physiological, vital-sign, nutritional, mental-health, and gynecological parameters—including heart rate, SpO2, breathing rate, optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD), cabin/suit CO2, bone mineral density loss, hydration, sleep stages, heart rate variability (HRV), reaction speed (PVT), diet, and menstrual or hormonal suppression health. Incoming data from daily 30-second check-ins, galley food logs, and simulated wearable/lab syncs is evaluated by a deterministic rules engine that:

- Adapts safe baselines dynamically to the crew member's current gravity, atmosphere, terrain dust, and thermal environment.

- Assigns both a clear Normal / Drift / Critical status and a directional 1–7 bipolar severity gauge.

- Applies "must last N days" persistence rules so single-day fluctuations in calorie intake or heavy menstrual flow do not trigger false alarms.

- Visualizes affected systems on an interactive 3D anatomical body map (with skin, muscle, skeleton, and organ layers) alongside 14D, 30D, 90D, and full-mission trend charts.

- Exports structured JSON telemetry snapshots for mission medical records.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

- Autonomous Deep-Space Safety: One-way radio delays between Mars and Earth reach up to 22 minutes (44 minutes round-trip), making real-time flight surgeon guidance impossible during acute events. Because A.R.T.E.M.I.S. runs 100% locally in any web browser with zero server dependency, crew members can diagnose early health drift and execute step-by-step countermeasures completely offline.

- Built for Non-Medical Crew: Most astronauts are engineers, pilots, and scientists rather than physicians. Instead of raw medical jargon, every metric includes plain-English explanations, a step-by-step visual diagram showing where to place each sensor, and a tap-to-explain glossary.

- Inclusive Space Medicine: Addresses critical gaps in female astronaut health by supporting both Mode A (pharmacological suppression—tracking pill compliance, breakthrough bleeding, and Galactic Cosmic Ray pill potency) and Mode B (natural cycle—tracking flow volume, cramping pain, and opposite dietary iron targets: >=18 mg/day during menstruation vs. <=8 mg/day cap under suppression to prevent microgravity neocytolysis iron toxicity).

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

- Location-Aware Equipment Intelligence: Rather than giving identical generic advice everywhere, the engine checks what medical hardware is actually available at the crew's location (for example, recognizing that a Lower Body Negative Pressure leg-vacuum chamber is available on a station or base, but not inside a compact lunar rover) and substitutes realistic field alternatives.

- Human-Factors Habit Loop: Combines a once-a-day check-in streak, time-based reminders, and a "Busy / Spacewalk Mode" streak freeze with a private CBT-guided reflection journal and 1- or 3-minute Psychomotor Vigilance Tests (PVT).

- Quiet-State & Accessible UI: Uses WCAG AA high-contrast styling and NASA-STD-3001 dual coding (combining geometric shapes—circle, triangle, octagon—with green, amber, and red status colors) so critical alerts remain unmistakable under high workload.

FACTORS OUR TEAM CONSIDERED

- Environmental Physics: Fractional gravity (0g, 0.166g, 0.38g), closed-loop ECLSS cabin/suit CO2 buildup, abrasive lunar regolith dust (8-OHdG), toxic Martian soil perchlorates, extreme external temperatures, and Galactic Cosmic Ray (GCR) / Solar Particle Event (SPE) radiation.

- Individual Physiology & Medical History: Sex-specific hydration and iron metabolism, baseline BMD T-scores, kidney-stone risk (+500 mL hydration buffer), SANS head-fluid sensitivity, clotting risk, and medication sensitivities (such as NSAID or iodine allergies).

- Behavioral & Cognitive Resilience: Circadian disruption, isolation stress, reaction-time degradation, and pelvic comfort/pain management during heavy EVA schedules.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

- Core Web Stack: Vanilla HTML5, CSS3, and modular JavaScript (metrics.js, engine.js, body3d.js, app.js) with zero build tools or backend server requirements.

- 3D Visualization & Asset Pipeline: Three.js (r147), GLTFLoader, RoomEnvironment, and Node.js with glTF-Transform and meshoptimizer to optimize the BodyParts3D anatomical mesh (CC BY 4.0) from ~3.5M triangles down to ~420k triangles (~4 MB) for fast browser rendering.

- Data Visualization & Storage: Chart.js (4.4.1) for multi-horizon trendlines, Plus Jakarta Sans typography, and browser localStorage for persistent offline state.

PROTOTYPE SCOPE & LIMITATIONS

This software is a functional hackathon prototype rather than a certified medical device. Wearable telemetry, lab assays, and galley nutrition values use simulated sample inputs; data is stored locally in one browser; and the 3D anatomy viewer uses an adult male reference model (with pelvic region targeting for female cycle metrics).
